_about: The negative-loop map the Alan app reads. Each loop links to evidence (library.json ids) and to a strategy drawn from Marquis's frameworks. Strategy wording is a DRAFT for Marquis to rewrite in his voice; it is not yet his approved language.

mindsetArchitecture.name: What you believe is possible
mindsetArchitecture.question: What do you quietly assume about what you can change?

mindsetArchitecture.name: Who you say you are
mindsetArchitecture.question: Which sentence about yourself do you act in line with, even when it costs you?

mindsetArchitecture.name: How you decide under pressure
mindsetArchitecture.question: What do you see first when stakes are high, and what do you miss?

mindsetArchitecture.name: How you handle the feeling
mindsetArchitecture.question: What do you do with the discomfort between wanting and doing?

mindsetArchitecture.name: Your operating system
mindsetArchitecture.question: What daily structure turns a decision into a repeated action?

loops.name: The story rewrite
loops.plain: You don't do the thing, so you change what you say you wanted.

strategy.move: Write the want and the last three actions side by side. Name the cheapest excuse your mind used to close the gap.

loops.name: The borrowed goal
loops.plain: You are chasing something someone else would be proud of.

strategy.move: For each goal ask whose voice is asking. Cut or rewrite any goal you would not choose if no one ever knew.

loops.name: The wish without the obstacle
loops.plain: You picture the finish line and skip the part in the middle.

strategy.move: Say the wish, then the real thing most likely to stop you this week. Decide whether to commit or release.

loops.name: The intention-action gap
loops.plain: You know what to do and still don't start.

strategy.move: Write one if-then plan: when this cue happens, I do this exact step.

loops.name: The replay loop
loops.plain: You go over the problem again and again without moving.

strategy.move: Swap 'why is this happening' for 'what is the next 15-minute step'. Refer out if this looks like depression.

loops.name: The defense reflex
loops.plain: Honest feedback feels like an attack, so you wave it off.

strategy.move: Start by naming a value you stand on, then look at the hard truth.

loops.name: The all-or-nothing reset
loops.plain: You miss a day and decide the whole thing is dead.

strategy.move: Plan the miss. Rule: never miss twice, and restart at the smallest version.
Turn the label into 'not yet' and attach one concrete practice, because belief alone moves little.

loops.name: The willpower myth
loops.plain: I ran out of willpower, so it's not my fault.

strategy.move: Redesign the environment and the cue instead of arguing with your tank. Don't promise clients a willpower-battery model.

loops.name: The harsh inner critic
loops.plain: You beat yourself up after a miss, believing that is what keeps you sharp.

strategy.move: After a miss, say what happened without a verdict, then name the next smallest step. Treat yourself the way you would a client you respect.

loops.name: The swallow-it loop
loops.plain: You push the feeling down and carry on, so it leaks out somewhere else.

strategy.move: Name the feeling in one sentence, then ask what else could be true about the situation. Pick one reframe you can act on today.

loops.name: The thought-is-a-fact loop
loops.plain: I feel I can't, so I can't.

strategy.move: Write the thought as 'I'm having the thought that...', then ask what you value here and take one step toward it anyway. Refer out if the distress is clinical.
